intro.title: Rotting Oranges
intro.body: In this lesson, you will implement an algorithm to simulate the rotting of oranges in a grid. You'll learn how to use a breadth-first search (BFS) approach to track the spread of rot across adjacent cells. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays for the grid and a queue data structure to manage the BFS process. This exercise will help you practice working with 2D arrays, queues, and iterative problem-solving in a step-by-step manner.
intro.usecase: The Rotting Oranges algorithm models propagation processes like network contagion in social platforms, where a post going viral spreads to connected users. It's used in infrastructure monitoring dashboards to visualize cascading failures in power grids or server clusters as outages ripple through connected nodes. Game developers apply this pattern for area-of-effect mechanics in strategy games, where environmental effects expand turn-by-turn. This BFS approach helps product teams build features that track how states change through connected systems over time.
